messages:
sara: fyi legal flagged a DSAR that asks for complete account erasure + cryptographic proof. request references an old snapshot id that might be affected by last year's KMS rotation. best approach?
legal-bot: New DSAR #540 created by user@example.com — requires deletion proof and timeline. SLA: 30d.
mike: thanks. first question: do we have an auditable chain from `delete-requests` service to snapshot purge? iirc snapshots live in GCS and are encrypted with customer KEK that we rotated in 2024.
dan: snapshots are encrypted with our service KEK (projects/redwood-keystore), rotated 2024-09. rotation created new key version, old keys are retained for decrypt until TTL. we do key rewraps for new uploads only. older snapshots still decrypt with old key versions until we schedule rewrap.
emma: so if we rotate and then later revoke old version, can we still prove deletion? legal wants evidence that the snapshot was removed and the associated key material destroyed or inaccessible.
mike: two layers: 1) object-level deletion in GCS (object removed) 2) KMS audit showing crypto key version state. we need both. GCS shows delete events in object access logs for the bucket. KMS logs show cryptoKeyVersion state changes.
sara: are those logs immutable/retained for the evidence window? legal will ask for tamper-proof timeline.
d an: audit logs are in Cloud Logging with 365d retention by default. but some projects have shorter retention; we keep long-term aggregates in cold storage, but detailed payloads might be truncated. ops-bot: Retention: project-prod-logs -> 365d, project-archive-logs -> indefinite (exported).
mike: we should export the exact log slices immediately to archive bucket with restricted ACLs and hash them (sha256) and include the hash in the DSAR response bundle. simple step: run export, compute `sha256sum` of the exported file, store proof in internal vault.
emma: question on RBAC: the deletion job runs as service-account `delete-runner@redwood-infra`. Legal wants to know who could have triggered deletion or overridden the job. we need a minimal list of principals with iam/roles that allow `storage.objects.delete` and `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.destroy`.
dan: current perms: `delete-runner` has `roles/storage.objectAdmin` on bucket and `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` at keystore. humans with `roles/owner` or `roles/editor` can obviously do dangerous ops. we recently gave `platform-oncall` `roles/storage.admin` for incident response — that expands deletion surface.
sara: can we produce a short RBAC matrix for the past 18 months and include a timestamped snapshot of IAM policy? legal will want who had the ability at the time of alleged access.
mike: yes — I can pull `gcloud projects get-iam-policy` historical via policy export snapshots we keep in `infra-policy-archive` (we've been exporting monthly). will attach policy for the month containing the snapshot creation and the deletion date.
emma: on KMS side, if we decide to rotate/disable old key versions to prove they can't decrypt, that's destructive and could impact forensic decrypts for other cases. legal usually accepts key version revocation logs as proof of inaccessibility without destroying all versions. can we do a non-destructive approach?
dan: propose: 1) confirm object delete event in storage logs 2) export KMS audit entries showing `cryptoKeyVersions.disable` or `setIamPolicy` changes 3) export key metadata showing key version states at archive 4) hash+store all exports in evidence bucket with ACL restricted to legal & sec.
sara: also, we need to flag a retention exception playbook because the snapshot referenced might be subject to a legal hold for an ongoing vulnerability investigation. legal just pinged that there was a potential leak — we must not purge anything until hold cleared.\legal-bot: Alert: Incident #981 (possible data exfil) is associated with DSAR #540. Legal hold requested by legal@redwood.com. Hold state: ACTIVE.
mike: ok hold supersedes deletion. we need to coordinate with vuln team to triage quickly. vuln team: can someone confirm if the referenced snapshot ID is in scope for incident 981?\sara: @dan can you check? if it's in scope, we must mark the snapshot as evidence and not delete. also record: who accessed snapshot, copy counts, and any downloads.
dan: checking... quick grep in audit exports: found `storage.objects.get` by service account `build-exporter@` near the timestamp in question. also found `storage.objects.copy` events. not conclusively exfil but needs deeper triage.
emma: if the snapshot is evidence, we need to change RBAC to lock down: remove broad `platform-oncall` storage.admin, create `forensics-viewer` role with read-only, and grant to a small list. any RBAC change must be recorded via change request and tagged to DSAR/incident IDs.
mike: agreed. small checklist for next steps:
- [ ] export storage delete/get/copy logs 30d window and hash
- [ ] export IAM policy snapshots for last 18 months
- [ ] export KMS key history (versions, disable/destroy events)
- [ ] if hold ACTIVE, mark snapshot as evidence label `evidence/incident-981` (add metadata)
- [ ] propose RBAC lockdown PR and route through change control
- [ ] draft DSAR response with attached hashed logs and policy artifacts
sara: I'll coordinate with legal for DSAR wording. mike/dan/emma — please do exports and post the signed hashes here. once we have it, legal will draft a response that references the audit hashes and the hold state.
dan: starting exports now, ETA ~2h. command I'm running: ```gcloud logging read 'resource.type="gcs_bucket" AND protoPayload.methodName:("storage.objects.delete" OR "storage.objects.copy" OR "storage.objects.get")' --start-time="2024-10-10T00:00:00Z" --end-time="2024-10-25T23:59:59Z" --format=json > /tmp/dsar_logs.json```\emma: thx. i'll open a quick PR to remove `platform-oncall` storage.admin and add `forensics-viewer` - label it `security/DSAR-540` so we have traceability.\ops-bot: NOTE: Any IAM changes will trigger an audit entry; ensure PR references DSAR/incident number for traceability.
sara: perfect. keep updates short. legal needs the artifacts by EOD.
mike: uploaded exports to `gs://evidence-exports/dsar-540/` and posted `sha256` in the secure vault. hash: `3f5c9e2b2a1d6...` (full hash in vault).\dan: added log snippet (redacted) showing copy event: \n```json\n{"protoPayload": {"methodName":"storage.objects.copy","authenticationInfo":{"principalEmail":"build-exporter@redwood-infra.iam.gserviceaccount.com"},"resourceName":"projects/_/buckets/snapshots/objects/snap-20240901.img"}}\n```
emma: PR created: #1428 - `security: DSAR 540 RBAC lockdown` - reviewers: sara, mike, dan.
sara: thanks. once PR merges, capture `setIamPolicy` audit entry and include in DSAR bundle.
legal-bot: DSAR #540 updated: evidence bundle received (partial). Next update requested 2024-10-25 17:00 UTC.
mike: will follow up after IAM change and final exports.
sara: closing loop: document this thread in case legal asks for chain of custody. tagging `legal/DSAR-540` and `incident/981` in the PR and the evidence bucket.
emma: noted. any objections to locking down platform-oncall temporarily?
dan: no objections. do it as emergency change with postmortem.
sara: go ahead. thanks team :thumbsup:
